title: The NRI's Guide to World Cup 2026 at Hard Rock Stadium, Miami
excerpt: 7 matches including Brazil vs Scotland and the Bronze Final, South Florida's best Indian restaurants from Fort Lauderdale to Weston, transit tips, and how the Sunshine State's growing desi community can attend the World Cup.
body:
Miami is hosting 7 World Cup matches — more than most cities — including marquee group games like Brazil vs Scotland and Colombia vs Portugal, plus a quarterfinal and the Bronze Final. Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens is the venue, and South Florida's growing Indian community is centered around Weston, Sunrise, and Fort Lauderdale.

## Where to Eat: South Florida Desi Spots

South Florida's Indian food scene is concentrated in Broward County — Davie, Sunrise, Weston, and Pembroke Pines — all within 20-30 minutes of Hard Rock Stadium.

**Bombay Darbar (4.7 stars, 579 reviews):** The go-to for upscale Indian in South Florida with locations in Fort Lauderdale (Las Olas Blvd), Coconut Grove, and Doral. Butter chicken, lamb chop masala, full bar, and outdoor seating.

**Palace Indian Restaurant** in Davie has an excellent buffet and the Palace Feast platter for groups. Himalayan Indian Kitchen in Pembroke Pines serves a Himalayan Thali ($52, shareable for two) with 4 curries, naan, rice, and desserts. Zaika Weston for modern Indian in a cozy upscale setting.

**Vegetarian/South Indian:** Woodlands Pure Vegetarian in Lauderhill/Sunrise is the South Indian institution — dosas, idli, vada, and weekday lunch buffet. Been serving the community for years.

**Street Food & Casual:** Nirala Sweets in Sunrise for Pakistani-Indian sweets, halal bihari kabobs, dum biryani, and weekend halwa puri breakfast. Indian Chillies in Lauderhill for street food vibes.

**For the finals splurge:** Bombay Darbar's Las Olas location in Fort Lauderdale is perfect for a special-occasion dinner — one of the best-reviewed Indian restaurants in all of Florida.

## Getting There

**Tri-Rail + Shuttle:** Take Tri-Rail from Fort Lauderdale or Miami stations to the nearest stop, then use FIFA match-day shuttles to the stadium. Check Tri-Rail's World Cup schedule for extended service.

**Driving & Parking:** Pre-purchase required at Hard Rock Stadium. Multiple lots available, but budget $75-150+ depending on the match. The stadium is right off the Florida Turnpike and I-75.

**Rideshare:** Fine for pre-match ($20-40 from Fort Lauderdale). Post-match surge pricing is guaranteed. Designated pickup/drop-off zones at the stadium.

**Brightline (from Downtown Miami):** Take Brightline to Aventura station, then shuttle or rideshare the last few miles to the stadium.

## Where to Stay

**Fort Lauderdale Beach (20 min):** Beach hotels plus Bombay Darbar on Las Olas Blvd. Good nightlife and walkability.

**Weston/Davie (20 min):** The NRI sweet spot — largest South Asian community in South Florida with Indian restaurants, grocery stores, and temples. Suburban feel, good for families.

**Aventura/Hallandale (15 min):** Aventura Mall, waterfront dining, Brightline station nearby. Good mid-point between Miami vibes and stadium access.

**Miami Beach/South Beach (30-45 min):** The glamour play. Classic Miami experience but farthest from the stadium. Best if combining World Cup with a vacation.

## Desi Community

**Shiva Mandir** in Oakland Park and the **Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Sanstha (BAPS)** in Bartlett Park serve the Hindu community. The Sunrise/Weston corridor is the center of South Florida's Indian population — Indian grocery stores, clothing shops, and community gathering spots along Oakland Park Blvd and University Dr.

**Sabka Bazaar** and other Indian grocery stores in Sunrise carry everything from fresh curry leaves to ready-made dosa batter.

## Tickets

Available at [FIFA.com/tickets](https://www.fifa.com/fifaplus/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/tickets). Brazil vs Scotland (Jun 24) and Colombia vs Portugal (Jun 27) will be the hottest group-stage tickets. The Quarterfinal (Jul 11) and Bronze Final (Jul 18) offer a chance to see the tournament's late-stage drama.
